recipes.name: Grilled Marinated Shrimp
ingredients_raw: 2 pounds large shrimp, peeled and deveined with tails attached

steps.text: Whisk olive oil, parsley, lemon juice, hot pepper sauce, garlic, tomato paste, oregano, salt, and black pepper together in a mixing bowl. Reserve a small amount for basting later.
Pour remaining marinade into a large resealable plastic bag; add shrimp, coat with the marinade, squeeze out excess air, and seal the bag. Marinate shrimp in the refrigerator for 2 hours.
Preheat a grill to medium-low heat. Thread shrimp onto skewers, piercing once near the tail and once near the head. Discard any remaining marinade.
Lightly oil the grill grate. Cook shrimp until opaque, about 5 minutes per side, basting frequently with reserved marinade.

raw_recipe.headline: Grilled Marinated Shrimp
raw_recipe.description: A simple shrimp marinade made with lemon, garlic, parsley, and hot sauce adds flavor to juicy shrimp grilled on skewers for a great summer meal.

review.reviewBody: This recipe is AWESOME!! I made it exactly as written, which I always try to do on the first go-round because that's only fair to the submitter. That way, I'm reviewing THE RECIPE and not my new version of it. Ticks me off when some reviewers completely change the recipe and then take off stars cause they didn't like it. OK, I'll get off my soapbox now!! DH RAVED about the shrimp!! And you're gonna think I'm crazy, but try this as a side dish: reserve some of the marinade (I saved about 1/2 cup) cut a head of romaine lengthwise, leaving the core on to hold the leaves together, and allowing 1/4 head per person, drizzle the reserved marinade over it and let it sit. When the shrimp are done, cover them with foil and then throw the romaine ON THE GRILL! Cook it, turning several times, until the leaves are wilted and browning a bit. Then, either serve as a whole quarter or chop to make a bed for the shrimp! Better than pasta, cause it's a nice, crisp complement to the juicy shrimp! Thank you, Robbie, for an excellent dinner last night!

I have found my finance & myself to be somewhat seafood snobs so to say. I say this because we have a beach house on the cost of Louisiana where we get the freshest seafood possible. The shrimp come striaght from the gulf into our home. We've tried close to a hundred different grilled seafood recipes & this recipe was absolutely fabulous. It wasnt spicy at all unless you hate spices, because I added a little cayenne to mine. We were short on time & I marinated for maybe 30 min., added a cinammon chiptle rub, & folks this marinade was great!! Its so quick & easy you can't beat it with a stick! Leave the lemon out if you're marinading for hrs. It makes the texture of the seafood horrible! Add it about 30min befoer grilling!

This is a staple recipe, highly requested. For my Hot sauce I will use scorpion Tabasco and 3 drops of flat line ghost pepper extract. Let it marinade overnight. The heat is spot on.... I'll also skip the hotsauce for those who don't do heat, still supper yummy. I have also used this recipe for the thin flank steaks for sandwiches. It is so good. Flavor isn't as strong, but it is there. 100% winner in my house

Hubby and I were looking for something yummy to cook shrimp in our air fryer. I didn't have much time to marinade the shrimp, probably gave it about 20 minutes, so I doubled the garlic, lemon, salt, pepper, and Cholula. This was SO FREAKING GOOD that I pulled out more shrimp and we're making more for later. I didn't have tomato paste, parsley, or oregano so we made this more of a lemon pepper shrimp. Thank you for sharing such a fantastic recipe!!

I’ve made it several times. I got tired of throwing away so much olive oil. I made two changes. Half cup of oil. Then use immersion blender. Marinate in gallon ziplock. Don’t need to baste. Careful not to overcook.

Reduced the amounts due to fewer shrimp. Cooked shrimp in wok with white onion and cherry tomatoes (sweated onion/tomato removed then combined with cooked shrimp). Put mixture on bed of rice noodles. Very tasty. Great marinade!

This has become a mainstay for our summer bbq parties, however 2 Tbsps of hot pepper sauce is too much for my family's taste. I reduced it to just 2 tsps and it is very good - still has some kick but not overpowering.

I have made this several times. Last night i cut the recipe in half for my husband and myself. I only added a couple shakes of Tobassco as he doesn’t like hot but he didn’t say anything so next time will give another couple! I only marinated 45 minutes without lemon and added it the last 15 so as not to cook shrimp. Also I had to broil as barbecue not ready for the season yet. Still very good!

The grill wasn't working, so I cooked it on 450 degrees for 6 minutes, following by a few minutes under the broiler. Came out great! I had already put the shrimp on skewers, so I used a 9 x 12 Pyrex baking dish as a rack. No need to turn them over.

This marinade makes absolutely the best tasting shrimp. My husband said it tasted even better than a restaurant's and we are going to use it as a weekly meal from now on. I used cayenne instead of hot pepper sauce and a little dried parsley, with my fresh parsley instead of oregano because I didn't have any on hand. We sautéd the shrimp on the stove and made tacos. Super good.

I made this for a group event of about 40 people. Everyone raved about this recipe. At least 5 men specifically came up to me and said this is the best shrimp they have ever ate. 
I did make 15 pounds of shrimp so I made 7 times the amount. I marinated the shrimp for 2 hours and didn't add the lemon juice till 30 minutes before. But I agree with many here. The Lemon juice starts "cooking" the ends of the shrimp and created a gummy coating. Again everyone loved it though. I will only marinade it for 30-45 minutes next time and add the lemon about 5-10 minutes before grilling. We put the veggies on separate skewers from the shrimp which worked really well.
Excellent marinades that is sure to be a WINNER! Husband asked for this to be added to monthly meal menu rotation.
Loved it!!!
Easy to make, and the tomato paste and hot sauce gave it great flavor. I marinated for 3 hours. Perfect
Oh my, this was amazing. I did wait until last 30 mins to add lemon but otherwise followed recipe and it was 5 star! I sent to all my fellow cookers!

I'm shocked there are so many 5-star reviews. I would only give this 1 star, but hubby said they were okay, so I'm giving it 2. I marinated them for about 1 hour and broiled them, instead of grilling them, for 2 minutes per side. They were overcooked and rubbery. I can only imagine how bad they would have been had I marinated them for 2 hours and grilled them for 10 minutes. I'm going back to my tried-and-true recipe. Alton Brown's Cocktail Shrimp. Served warm or chilled, they are 1000 times better than this!!
My family and I love this recipe. Easy and quick on the bbq.

I followed the recipe exactly as written, except I doubled it (and added lemon zest), and I'm glad I did! Not only was it delicious with shrimp, but we also marinated chicken with it. Both were spectacular. I also marinated some zucchini, onions, and cauliflower in it and that went on the grill as well. I made some chickpea pasta and mixed it with sauteed onions and peppers and the remaining marinade, and ended up throwing the grilled vegetables into the saute pan to marry it all together. Just wonderful! And hats off to the reviewer who had the idea to spoon out tablespoons of the tomato paste onto waxed paper and freeze. I only had a big can of paste, and I was glad to not have it go to waste. This was a wonderful recipe that we will be using often!
It's awesome!

Quite a few ingredients in the marinade, but the end result is well worth the effort! I only marinated for 30 minutes. Due to the lemon juice (acid), I didn't want the shrimp to start "cooking", which tends to happen with longer marinating times. I used extra jumbo sized shrimp which are 16-20 shrimp per pound - a perfect size to fit all the shrimp on 6 skewers. I will make this again!
